---
title: Import
---

## Import a recipe

Turn any recipe into a Gram draft: paste the raw recipe text below, or give a web link — the page fetches it, extracts schema.org Recipe JSON-LD when available (falling back to plain-text parsing), and converts quantities to grams/millilitres. Anything the static parser couldn't handle confidently is tagged below the draft — those are the spots where an AI translation pass would help.

For higher-fidelity AI-assisted conversion from a URL or YouTube video, use the CLI instead: `npx gram import <url> --pick-model` (needs an AI provider key).

<form id="import-form" class="import-form">
  <label for="import-url">Recipe URL</label>
  <input id="import-url" type="url" placeholder="https://example.com/recipe" />
  <label for="import-text">…or paste the raw recipe text</label>
  <textarea id="import-text" rows="8" placeholder="# Recipe title

## Ingredients

- 200 g tofu
- 2 cups spinach

## Instructions

1. Fry the tofu."></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Convert to Gram</button>
</form>

<p id="import-status" role="status"></p>

<div id="import-tags" class="import-tags" hidden></div>

<div id="import-output" hidden>
  <h3>Gram draft (<code>.gram</code>)</h3>
  <textarea id="import-preview" rows="18" spellcheck="false"></textarea>
  <div class="import-actions">
    <button id="import-download" type="button">Download .gram</button>
    <button id="import-copy" type="button">Copy to clipboard</button>
  </div>
  <p>Save the file as <code>sources/&lt;slug&gt;.gram</code>, add missing ingredients to <code>.gram/ingredients.yaml</code>, then run <code>npx gram check "sources/**/*.gram"</code> and rebuild.</p>
</div>
